answer: Cap the weight any identity can receive at the min-cut of attestation edges reaching a bounded horizon of established non-kin anchors. A farm is one dense lotus of clones rooted together, sharing only thin edges to that horizon, so its weight stays pinned to that narrow cut however many clones it spins up. Each genuine edge to the horizon costs real separately-earned standing a farm cannot print, so cost grows per identity and cannot be pooled across operators. Clones with no such edge stay in a sable region the cut isolates and down-weights. Failure: an isolated newcomer is under-weighted.
